items.title: Animal Mirror Parade
items.summary: Take turns leading silly animal movements while everyone mirrors the leader.
setupSteps: Clear a small safe space for walking and wiggling.
playSteps: Choose one leader.
The leader moves like an animal while everyone copies.
Switch leaders after three animals.
items.parentNotes: Use gentle movements for younger children and avoid jumping near furniture.
variations: Whisper the animal for a quiet round.
Let each child invent a brand-new animal.

items.title: Couch Cushion Quest
items.summary: A tiny indoor scavenger hunt using safe household clues.
setupSteps: Use this ready-made set: one couch cushion, one shoe, and one book. Place them in view and within easy reach.
playSteps: Read Clue 1: “Find something soft that rests on the couch.”
Read Clue 2: “Find something you wear on your foot.”
Read Clue 3: “Find something with pages that tells a story.”
Children point to or fetch each matching object; celebrate every find with a silly cheer.
items.parentNotes: Keep objects visible for younger children.
variations: Use colors only.
Use rhyming clues for older children.

items.title: Alphabet Story
items.summary: Build a ready-to-start family story with the next letter of the alphabet.
setupSteps: Sit where everyone can hear; begin with A, or use the shorter A-through-F round.
playSteps: Adult reads the ready-made start: “A tiny alligator found a bright balloon.”
Continue with B: “Bouncy bears brought blueberry biscuits.”
Continue with C: “Curious cats came closer.”
Then take turns with D, E, and F; short phrases, sounds, or one word all count.
Finish the story after F, or keep going through the alphabet if everyone wants more.
items.parentNotes: Offer the sample sentence or a word beginning with the next letter so no child has to invent alone.
variations: Ready animal round: alligator, bear, cat, dog, elephant, frog.
Ready food round: apple, banana, carrot, doughnut, egg, fruit.
For ages 2–3, say the next letter and animal together; the child can make its sound.

items.title: Freeze Dance Statues
items.summary: Dance, freeze, and pose as funny statues.
setupSteps: Clear a safe dance space.
playSteps: Parent claps a rhythm or plays family-approved music outside the app.
Everyone dances.
When the parent says freeze, everyone becomes a statue.
items.parentNotes: Keep movement gentle and stop before children get too wild.
variations: Freeze as animals.
Freeze as superheroes.

items.title: Pillow Boat Adventure
items.summary: Pretend pillows are boats crossing a living-room sea.
setupSteps: Place pillows on the floor with walking space between them.
playSteps: Pretend the floor is water.
Step from boat to boat slowly.
Name friendly sea creatures you see.
items.parentNotes: No jumping. Keep pillows flat and stable.
variations: Make it a quiet tiptoe adventure.
Add a stuffed animal passenger.

items.title: Calm Cloud Breaths
items.summary: A short breathing reset using imaginary clouds.
setupSteps: Sit or stand comfortably.
playSteps: Pretend to hold a fluffy cloud.
Smell the cloud slowly.
Blow it gently across the sky.
Repeat three times.
items.parentNotes: Keep the tone soft and brief.
variations: Use pretend flower breaths.
Use pretend cocoa breaths.

items.title: I Spy
items.summary: Play the familiar I Spy guessing game with ready-made color and shape rounds.
setupSteps: Choose one safe object everyone can see; use the ready-made clues below if you are tired.
playSteps: The adult starts: “I spy with my little eye something blue.”
Players point or guess until someone finds a blue object.
Continue with something round, something soft, something red, and something tiny but visible.
Let the next player choose one of those same clues or name a new visible object.
items.parentNotes: Keep every object visible and use pointing instead of fetching in waiting rooms.
variations: Color round: blue, red, yellow, green, then purple.
Shape round: circle, square, triangle, rectangle, then star.
Quiet round: everyone points instead of calling out.

items.title: Moon Pancake Mission
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly space breakfast story.

madLibs.template: Captain {name} flew a {adjective} rocket to the moon to deliver {food}. When the hatch opened, a moon {animal} shouted {sound}! Everyone laughed and shared breakfast among the stars.

items.title: Dragon Laundry Day
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a dragon helping with chores.

madLibs.template: The {color} dragon found a tiny {object} in the laundry basket. It tried to {verb} it clean, but accidentally made {number} bubbles float through the house.

items.title: Backyard Castle News
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a royal announcement from a pretend castle.

madLibs.template: Breaking news from the castle of {place}: the royal {adjective} {noun} has been found by a brave {animal}. The kingdom will celebrate with extra giggles tonight.

items.title: If Toys Could Talk
items.summary: Imagine what a favorite toy would say.
items.promptText: Pick a toy nearby. If it could talk for one minute, what would it ask your family?
followUps: What adventure would it want next?

items.title: Tiny Kindness Plan
items.summary: Think of one small kind thing to do today.
items.promptText: What is one tiny kind thing we can do for someone in our family today?
followUps: Can we do it in less than two minutes?

items.title: Charades
items.summary: Play familiar charades with ready-to-act animal, activity, and sports ideas.
setupSteps: Clear a small safe movement space.
playSteps: Choose a ready idea: cat, elephant, brushing teeth, stirring soup, kicking a ball, or swimming.
Act it out without words while everyone guesses.
The first guesser takes the next turn, or the adult chooses and acts together with younger children.
items.parentNotes: For younger kids, whisper the animal and act together.
variations: Animals: cat, elephant, frog, penguin, rabbit, or turtle.
Activities: brushing teeth, stirring soup, reading a book, sweeping, or sleeping.
Sports: kicking a ball, swimming, skating, basketball, or tennis; mime gently in place.

items.title: Would You Rather
items.summary: Choose between ready-to-read, harmless silly options and explain why.
items.promptText: Would you rather have pancakes for shoes or spaghetti for hair for one silly day?
followUps: What would be the funniest part?
Would your answer change for just one minute?
variations: Gross & Silly — Would you rather sneeze bubbles or burp tiny trumpet sounds?
Gross & Silly — Would you rather have noodles for hair or soft green peas for toes?
Gross & Silly — Would you rather brush furry teeth or comb a very stinky sock?
Gross & Silly — Would you rather hiccup “pickle” or pass a tiny squeaky toot whenever you laugh?

items.title: Timed Drawing: Tiny Monster
items.summary: Draw a friendly tiny monster before the timer ends.
setupSteps: Give each child paper and a safe drawing tool.
Set a one-minute timer outside the app or count slowly together.
playSteps: Draw a friendly tiny monster.
Add one silly detail after time ends.
Let each child name their monster.
items.parentNotes: No judging art quality; the goal is fast playful creativity.
variations: Draw a robot, snack creature, or castle pet.

items.title: Sock Skating Rink
items.summary: Slide carefully on socks across a pretend tiny rink.
setupSteps: Use only a smooth, clear floor area and remove obstacles.
playSteps: Stand with feet close and take tiny sliding steps.
Parent calls out slow skating shapes: circle, line, stop.
Finish with a silly statue pose.
items.parentNotes: Skip this on slippery or crowded floors; small steps only.
variations: Make it silent skating.
Pretend to deliver cocoa to stuffed animals.

items.title: Stuffed Animal Rescue
items.summary: Rescue plush friends from safe spots around the room.
setupSteps: Place a bear beside the couch, a bunny visibly under the table edge, and a puppy beside a pillow; keep the walking path clear.
playSteps: Rescue 1: Bear is stranded beside the couch. Walk over, carry Bear gently to base, and check both paws.
Rescue 2: Bunny is waiting under the table edge. Crawl only if the adult says the space is clear, bring Bunny to base, and offer a pretend carrot.
Rescue 3: Puppy is lost beside a pillow. Follow three quiet barks, bring Puppy to base, and tuck Puppy under the pillow like a blanket.
items.parentNotes: Keep hiding spots visible for younger children.
variations: Pointing round: point to Bear, Bunny, and Puppy in order instead of walking.
Color-clue round: rescue the brown bear, white bunny, then spotted puppy, or name the colors of your own toys.

items.title: Kitchen Band Rehearsal
items.summary: Make a gentle rhythm band with safe household items.
setupSteps: Choose non-breakable items and set a soft volume rule.
playSteps: Parent taps a simple beat.
Children copy the beat.
Each child gets one short solo.
End with a quiet final note.
items.parentNotes: No glass, sharp tools, or loud banging.
variations: Use claps only.
Play fast, slow, loud, and quiet rounds.

items.title: Blanket Fort Post Office
items.summary: Deliver pretend mail between cozy stations.
setupSteps: Build a simple blanket fort or choose two chairs as stations.
Use a separate paper scrap for each ready-made note, or read each note aloud for a child to decorate.
Copy Mail 1: You make me smile.
Copy Mail 2: Please do three silly wiggles.
Copy Mail 3: A big hug is waiting at the fort.
playSteps: Deliver Mail 1 to the fort; the receiver reads or repeats the smile message.
Deliver Mail 2 to the second station; everyone does three silly wiggles.
Deliver Mail 3 back to the fort; offer a hug, high five, or friendly wave.
items.parentNotes: Help younger children decorate or deliver the supplied notes instead of writing.
variations: Picture-only round: draw a smile, three wiggly lines, and a heart on the three notes.
Quiet round: point to each picture instead of reading the note aloud.

items.title: Teddy Bear Doctor
items.summary: Run a pretend checkup for stuffed animals.
setupSteps: Gather one or two stuffed animals.
playSteps: Ask what the animal needs.
Check ears, paws, and heartbeat with pretend tools.
Prescribe hugs, rest, or a silly song.
items.parentNotes: Keep the tone gentle and reassuring.
variations: Make a waiting room.
Older kids create patient charts.

items.title: Shape Detective
items.summary: Search the room for circles, squares, and triangles.
setupSteps: Pick a room with visible safe objects.
playSteps: Parent names a shape.
Children point to matching objects.
Count how many shapes you found.
items.parentNotes: Good for waiting or transitions.
variations: Use textures instead.
Older kids combine shape plus color.

items.title: Pirate Map Steps
items.summary: Follow a tiny pretend map using steps and turns.
setupSteps: Copy this ready-made map on paper: X (start) → couch → doorway → table (treasure). Keep the walking path clear.
playSteps: Start at X, then take four tiny steps to the couch.
Turn right, take three tiny steps toward the doorway, turn left, then take four tiny steps to the table.
At the table, choose the treasure you found: a golden banana, a sparkling seashell, or a tiny dragon egg.
items.parentNotes: Keep routes clear and slow.
variations: Use a verbal map only.
Let each child draw one stop.

items.title: Whisper Zoo
items.summary: Create a quiet zoo using animal whispers and gentle poses.
setupSteps: Sit or stand in a comfortable spot.
playSteps: Parent names a quiet animal.
Everyone makes its smallest sound.
Hold a gentle animal pose for five seconds.
items.parentNotes: Useful when the room needs to stay calm.
variations: Use underwater animals.
Use bedtime animals.

items.title: Rainbow Sort Sprint
items.summary: Sort safe toys or blocks by color in a short timed challenge.
setupSteps: Choose items too large to swallow and clear a sorting space.
playSteps: Pick three colors.
Sort items into color groups.
Count each group together.
items.parentNotes: Avoid small items around toddlers.
variations: Sort by size.
Make a quiet no-timer version.

items.title: Family News Desk
items.summary: Report happy family news from a pretend desk.
setupSteps: Choose a pretend microphone object or use empty hands.
playSteps: Parent gives a headline: Something kind happened today.
Each child reports one sentence.
End with a pretend weather report for the room.
items.parentNotes: Coach shy kids with sentence starters.
variations: Report from outer space.
Interview a stuffed animal.

items.title: Five Senses Tour
items.summary: Notice safe sights, sounds, and textures in the room.
setupSteps: Sit together or walk slowly.
playSteps: Name five things you see.
Name four sounds or quiet spots.
Touch three safe textures.
Take one slow breath.
items.parentNotes: Skip taste and smell unless a parent chooses safe options.
variations: Do only three senses.
Make it a bedtime tour.

items.title: Cleanup Countdown Game
items.summary: Turn a tiny cleanup into a cooperative mission.
setupSteps: Choose a small, safe cleanup zone.
playSteps: Parent picks five items to put away.
Count down from five together.
Celebrate when the tiny mission is complete.
items.parentNotes: Keep it small so it feels successful.
variations: Sort by person.
Use robot voices.

items.title: Paper Airplane Weather
items.summary: Test paper airplanes through gentle pretend weather.
setupSteps: Fold the paper in half lengthwise, crease it, and unfold it. Fold both top corners to the center crease, then fold the new slanted edges to the center crease.
Fold the plane in half lengthwise with the folded edges outside. Fold each wing down so its long top edge meets the bottom folded edge, then open both wings until they are flat.
Adult clears a throwing lane away from faces, stairs, pets, and fragile items.
playSteps: Fly once in calm weather.
Fly once during pretend wind.
Compare which flight went farther.
items.parentNotes: Throw away from faces and fragile items.
variations: Use crumpled paper comets.
Make prediction tickets before each flight.

items.title: Copycat Clap Code
items.summary: Repeat three supplied clap patterns from easy to tricky.
setupSteps: Sit where everyone can see hands.
playSteps: Pattern 1: clap-clap-pause-clap. The adult performs it slowly, then everyone copies it twice.
Pattern 2: clap-pause-clap-clap. The adult performs it slowly, then everyone copies it twice.
Pattern 3: clap-clap-clap-pause-clap. Copy it once slowly and once at a comfortable speed.
items.parentNotes: Keep patterns short for younger kids.
variations: Tap knees instead.
Use whisper words between claps.

items.title: Backyard Micro Safari
items.summary: Look for tiny outdoor details with parent supervision.
setupSteps: Choose a safe yard, porch, or window view.
playSteps: Find one leaf, one shadow, and one tiny movement.
Describe each discovery.
Leave plants and bugs undisturbed.
items.parentNotes: Hands-off observing only unless parent approves.
variations: Do it from a window.
Draw the best discovery afterward.

items.title: Chair Train Station
items.summary: Make chairs into a pretend train and announce stops.
setupSteps: Place stable chairs safely with walking space.
playSteps: Everyone boards, stays seated, and makes two gentle chug sounds.
Stop 1: Teddy Bear Town. Wave to three bears and say, “Tickets, please!”
Stop 2: Dinosaur Park. Make one soft roar and point to a pretend tall dinosaur.
Stop 3: Moon Station. Move your arms as if floating, then count down 3, 2, 1 for the ride home.
items.parentNotes: No climbing or standing on chairs.
variations: Use floor cushions instead.
Let older kids be conductors.

items.title: Memory Tray Peek
items.summary: Look at safe objects, hide them, and remember what changed.
setupSteps: Place three to five safe objects on a tray.
playSteps: Everyone looks for ten seconds.
Cover the tray.
Remove one object and reveal the tray.
Guess what changed.
items.parentNotes: Use large objects if toddlers are nearby.
variations: Start with two objects.
Older kids rearrange the tray.

items.title: Emotion Weather Report
items.summary: Describe feelings as weather and choose a next step.
setupSteps: Sit somewhere comfortable.
playSteps: Parent asks: what is your inside weather?
Choose sunny, cloudy, stormy, windy, or calm.
Pick one helpful action: hug, breath, water, quiet, or talk.
items.parentNotes: Do not force sharing; offer choices.
variations: Use colors instead of weather.
Draw the weather after talking.

items.title: Tiny Tower Engineers
items.summary: Build a small stable tower and test gentle changes.
setupSteps: Choose safe building pieces and a flat surface.
playSteps: Build the tallest tower that still stands.
Change one thing and test again.
Name the tower design.
items.parentNotes: Keep pieces away from mouths.
variations: Build the widest tower.
Make a team tower with one piece per turn.

items.title: Family Recipe Pretend
items.summary: Perform a complete silly no-cook Rainbow Dragon Soup recipe out loud.
setupSteps: Sit together and announce the supplied pretend dish: Rainbow Dragon Soup. No real food or cooking is required.
playSteps: Add two cloud puffs to the pretend bowl.
Add three rainbow noodles and one spoonful of moon peas.
Stir three times, whisper “sparkle, sparkle, soup,” and serve one pretend spoonful to each player.
items.parentNotes: Keep food allergy talk gentle if it comes up.
variations: Bedtime Moon Soup: add one moonbeam, two pillow puffs, and three sleepy stars; stir twice and whisper “good night.”
Dinosaur Crunch: add two fern leaves, three pebble crackers, and one volcano sprinkle; stomp once before serving.

items.title: Hallway Balance Beam
items.summary: Walk a pretend balance line with careful slow steps.
setupSteps: Choose a clear path and identify a pretend line.
playSteps: Walk heel-to-toe slowly.
Freeze at the end.
Return with tiny penguin steps.
items.parentNotes: No running or raised surfaces.
variations: Use a tape line if parent approves.
Carry a stuffed animal safely.

items.title: Quiet Library Helper
items.summary: Sort books or toys into tiny groups with whisper voices.
setupSteps: Choose a small pile of books or toys.
playSteps: Whisper-sort by size, color, or favorite.
Make one neat stack.
Pick one item to talk about softly.
items.parentNotes: Use only a few items to avoid overwhelm.
variations: Sort stuffed animals.
Create a bedtime shelf.

items.title: Best Part Today
items.summary: Share one good moment from the day.
items.promptText: What was one good part of today, even if it was tiny?
followUps: Would you want to do it again?

items.title: Helping Superpower
items.summary: Invent a superpower that helps someone.
items.promptText: If you had one helping superpower for ten minutes, what would it do?
followUps: What would your hero name be?

items.title: Kind Robot Instructions
items.summary: Give a robot kind, silly instructions.
items.promptText: A tiny robot wants to be helpful. What three kind jobs should it do?
followUps: What job should it not do?

items.title: Three Word Story
items.summary: Make a story from only three chosen words.
items.promptText: Choose three words and make the shortest story you can with all of them.
followUps: Can someone else add one sentence?
Can you make it gentler or sillier?

items.title: Thank-You Detective
items.summary: Notice someone to thank today.
items.promptText: Who did something helpful or kind today that we can thank?
followUps: How could we say thank you?

items.title: Silly Invention Pitch
items.summary: Pitch a harmless invention for family life.
items.promptText: Invent something silly that would make family life more fun. What is it called?

items.title: Wizard Pajama Parade
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a sleepy parade.

madLibs.template: Professor {name} announced the first {color} pajama parade. A tiny {animal} led the march and shouted {sound} every time someone yawned.
madLibs.readAloudNote: Read it with a sleepy announcer voice.

items.title: Robot Cookie Factory
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a robot baking pretend cookies with a surprise.

madLibs.template: The {adjective} robot opened a factory for {food}. It pressed one button and {number} tiny {object}s danced across the counter.

items.title: Undersea Bedtime Bus
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a bus driving under the sea at bedtime.

madLibs.template: The bedtime bus was driven by a sleepy {animal}. It stopped at {place}, flashed its {color} lights, and whispered {sound} to the fish.

items.title: Castle Pizza Problem
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a castle feast needing a strange solution.

madLibs.template: The royal {noun} refused to eat the {adjective} {food} until everyone agreed to {verb} around the table one time.
madLibs.readAloudNote: Read it as a royal decree.

items.title: Space Pet Show
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about pets competing in a zero-gravity show.

madLibs.template: Judge {name} welcomed the space {animal} show. The winner floated {adverb} through the ring and made a proud {sound}.

items.title: Breakfast Dragon Train
items.summary: Choose words to create and read a silly story about a dragon train delivering breakfast.

madLibs.template: The {color} dragon train delivered {food} to the {place}. It rang its bell {number} times and served everyone a plate of giggles.
madLibs.readAloudNote: Make the train bell sound gentle.

items.title: Animal Guessing
items.summary: Guess a ready-to-use animal by asking familiar yes-or-no questions.
setupSteps: Choose the first secret animal from cat, elephant, frog, penguin, rabbit, or turtle.
playSteps: The adult secretly chooses one animal from the list.
Players ask yes-or-no questions: “Does it have fur?”, “Can it swim?”, “Is it bigger than a chair?”, or “Does it hop?”
After three questions, each player may guess once; reveal the animal and choose another from the list.
items.parentNotes: For ages 2–3, show two choices and make the animal sounds together.
variations: Farm round: cow, chicken, horse, pig, sheep, or duck.
Ocean round: whale, shark, octopus, crab, turtle, or fish.
Movement round: crawl, hop, waddle, swim, stomp, or slither before guessing.

items.title: Race Like an Animal
items.summary: Cross a short course like an animal in a safe, flat, clear area.
setupSteps: Adult chooses a short, flat, clear area away from roads, stairs, furniture, and obstacles.
Mark a start and finish with existing landmarks; explain that it is a playful crossing, not a contact race.
playSteps: Round 1: hop gently like a kangaroo.
Round 2: take quick small steps like a cheetah without sprinting.
Round 3: make small rabbit hops, then squat and rise like a frog without leaping forward.
Everyone finishes one round before the next begins; stop if the area becomes crowded.
items.parentNotes: Use the walking/low-impact option for younger children or anyone who prefers it: walk while making the animal pose, with no hopping or running.
variations: Walking safari: walk like each animal from start to finish.
Call-and-copy: the adult demonstrates one low-impact movement and everyone follows.

items.title: Pillow Marco Polo: Eyes-Open Islands
items.summary: A safe eyes-open call-and-response walk using pillows only as island boundary markers.
setupSteps: Adult supervises and clears a flat room away from stairs, furniture edges, cords, pets, fragile objects, and other hazards.
Place two or three firm pillows flat as stationary island or boundary markers with wide walking space between them.
Safety rule: no throwing pillows, face covering, piling, jumping, running, blindfolds, or closing eyes.
playSteps: Everyone’s eyes remain open and all players walk only.
The adult is the stationary caller beside an island and says “Marco”; walkers answer “Polo.”
The adult names a visible island color or location; walkers move toward it and stop beside, not on, the pillow.
Switch the stationary caller after three slow rounds; stop if anyone feels unsure or play becomes chaotic.
items.parentNotes: Pillows are boundary/island markers only: never throw them, cover a face, pile them, or jump on them. Keep one arm of space between players.
variations: One-on-one quiet round: whisper “Marco” and “Polo” while walking between two islands.
Low-impact pointing round: stay stationary and point to the named island instead of walking.

items.title: Washable Coloring Together
items.summary: Share a simple coloring page with washable, non-toxic art tools and adult supervision.
setupSteps: Adult supervises, checks that crayons or markers are labeled washable and non-toxic, and covers the work surface for protection.
Draw one large circle, square, and triangle on the paper, or use the ready pattern: circle, square, triangle, circle.
playSteps: Each person chooses one shape and colors it.
Swap colors and add dots, stripes, or zigzags to the next shape.
Name the colors and shapes together, then display or recycle the finished page.
items.parentNotes: Supervise young children; art tools stay out of mouths and are put away when finished.
variations: Use only warm colors.
Take turns adding one mark to a shared rainbow.

items.title: Washable Painting Shapes
items.summary: Paint ready-made shapes with washable, non-toxic paint, protected surfaces, and adult supervision.
setupSteps: Adult supervises, confirms the children’s paint is washable and non-toxic, and covers the work surface and floor for protection.
Put out a small amount of paint, brushes, paper, water, and a cloth; draw a large circle, square, and triangle.
playSteps: Paint the circle with dots, the square with stripes, and the triangle with zigzags.
Trade brushes or colors and add one shape to each other’s page.
Place paintings flat to dry, close the paint, and wash hands and the protected surface together.
items.parentNotes: Supervise continuously; keep paint and rinse water out of mouths and clean spills promptly.
variations: Make a shape family with faces.
Use one color and mix lighter or darker shapes.
